scanWindow: Since the 2026-09-11 completed scan, plus material missed developments from the previous 48 hours
notes: Completed the 2026-09-12 editorial scan and published one Daily Brief. Anthropic's September 10 Threat Intelligence report had been held in the previous scan because the corresponding primary report was not reliably accessible; the primary report is now directly available from Anthropic, clearing the evidence bar. The brief focuses on the durable security signal rather than sensational examples: Anthropic says AI-enabled cyber tradecraft has diffused across actor classes, that a majority of the cyber operations in its case set used AI for direct execution or orchestration, and that some observed multi-agent frameworks performed reconnaissance, exploitation and data exfiltration with humans retaining target selection and review. These are Anthropic's observations from notable disrupted cases, not a prevalence estimate for all cyber activity. Reuters is retained as independent context. Mistral and Cloudera's sovereign-enterprise-AI partnership scored Worth knowing on primary evidence but is primarily a deployment/distribution partnership and did not displace the stronger security story. Reuters reporting that U.S. Senate negotiators are considering an AI duty-of-care regime scored highly on potential impact but remains Watch because negotiations are unfinished and no stable primary legislative text was established in this scan. Reuters reporting on a possible NVIDIA anchor investment in an Anthropic IPO also remains Watch because it is deal-talk reporting without company confirmation. A New Mexico sanctions case involving fabricated ChatGPT-generated legal material was logged but skipped as another instance of the established verification failure pattern rather than a new AI capability or governance development. OpenAI's September 10 government-access expansion was deduplicated against the prior scan. No rumours, unsupported rankings, unverified pricing or unsourced claims were published.
